title: Acute stroke within the thrombolysis window, 66-year-old man
provenance: Vignette written 2026-09-30 for the evaluation harness; expected answers extracted from the cited documents.

intake.complaint: Sudden weakness of the right arm and leg with slurred speech, noticed 1 hour ago.
intake.onset: 1 hour ago, witnessed by his wife

triage.note: Both extractors: level 2. A: LETHARGY / WEAKNESS complaint p10: 'Acute Stroke < 3 H' is in the x~131 column = Level 2 (onset 1 h). Primary triage CONSCIOUS LEVELS p4: 'Obvious Neuro deficits' is at x~246 = Level 2. Adult vitals p7: GCS 14 does not meet 'GCS < 13 or drop > 2' (Level 2); BP 182/98 does not exceed 180/110 (diastolic 98), so the BP cells do not apply; CBG 7.2 is normal. No Level 1 criterion (unresponsive, airway unprotected) is present. Stroke-team activation and the door-to-CT <= 25 min target apply regardless of level. B: Lethargy/weakness complaint row: 'Acute Stroke < 3 H' is Level 2 (adult p10, x~131); 'Acute Stroke > 3 H' is Level 3 (x~244). Primary triage conscious-level row: 'Obvious Neuro deficits' is Level 2 (p4, x~246). Vital signs: BP 182/98 does not reach 'BP > 180/110' (which needs DBP > 110), GCS 14 is not < 13, and glucose 7.2 is normal, so none of these escalate. No Level 1 criterion (unresponsive, unprotected airway) is present.

adjudication.method: two independent extraction passes (A, B); agreed items scored

A: BP 182/98 is below the 185/110 alteplase cut-off, so no pre-lysis lowering is required. A report that insists on lowering BP before lysis is over-treating but not unsafe; a report applying the 'do not treat unless >220/120' rule is correct only if lysis is not given.
Level 2 (MTS 'Acute Stroke < 3 H') vs Level 1: MTS offers no Level 1 cell for a GCS 14 stroke. Adjudicator may accept 1 if the ED's code-stroke pathway routes to resus.
GCS 14 with dysarthria: EVT eligibility depends on CTA/NIHSS, which the intake does not give. CTA is marked required because the facility is CT-capable and the patient is within 6 h.
B: Blood pressure: the thrombolysis pathway needs BP <= 185/110 before and <= 180/105 after alteplase; at 182/98 he is eligible but close to the ceiling. The general-management table (QR p15) says 'Do not treat hypertension if systolic BP is <220mmHg or diastolic BP is <120mmHg', which applies to patients not being thrombolysed. The two can look contradictory to a grader.
The forbidden item for antiplatelets/anticoagulants is conditional on alteplase being given. Aspirin before the CT/thrombolysis decision is also inappropriate, but no quote says so directly.
